S1_DEFECT_REPRODUCED.verdict: REPRODUCED. The defect is real, mechanical and fully determined by the scanner the repository already ships.

SCANNER_EVASION_MEASURED_AND_PROHIBITED.mechanism: db/hosted/baseline-scanner.ts classifies DML with the STATEMENT-INITIAL regex /^(INSERT|UPDATE|DELETE|COPY|TRUNCATE|MERGE)\b/i. A statement whose FIRST token is anything else is not classified as DML however much DML it performs.

measured_evasions.C_DO_BLOCK: `DO $$ BEGIN UPDATE ... ; END $$;` -> dmlStatements=0, literalRowSources=0. The scanner sees a statement beginning with DO. EVADES CLASSIFICATION.
measured_evasions.D_CTE_WRAPPED: `WITH first_member AS (SELECT ...) UPDATE ... FROM first_member ...` -> dmlStatements=0, literalRowSources=0. The scanner sees a statement beginning with WITH. EVADES CLASSIFICATION.

SCANNER_EVASION_MEASURED_AND_PROHIBITED.PROHIBITED_FORMS: The S1 implementing mission MUST NOT express the MO-11 backfill as, or relocate it into, ANY of: a DO block; a WITH ... UPDATE / WITH ... INSERT / WITH ... DELETE construction; a function body; a trigger body; or a dynamic EXECUTE string - WHEN DOING SO MAKES THE SCANNER'S CLASSIFICATION FALSE. Each of these makes a governed, disclosed structural backfill invisible to the very control this function exists to advance, converting an honest whitelist entry into a hidden write.
SCANNER_EVASION_MEASURED_AND_PROHIBITED.why_this_prohibition_is_load_bearing: Without it, the cheapest way to satisfy every gate in this addendum is to hide the UPDATE inside a DO block, leave all three controls untouched, and report a clean diff. That path is now explicitly PROHIBITED and is a STOP, not an optimisation.
SCANNER_EVASION_MEASURED_AND_PROHIBITED.not_a_scanner_defect_to_fix_here: The statement-initial anchor is a KNOWN, RECORDED limitation of the scanner. This addendum does NOT authorise changing db/hosted/baseline-scanner.ts, does not treat the limitation as a bug this lane may close, and carries it forward as an open finding instead.

THE_ID.byte_identical: The appended id MUST be BYTE-IDENTICAL in all three files. A divergence of even one character between the three is a STOP, not a typo to reconcile, because it would mean two of the three controls are asserting against a unit that does not exist.
THE_ID.must_equal_the_actual_unit_id: It MUST equal the actual S1 baseline unit id as registered in db/hosted/baseline-manifest.ts BASELINE_UNITS - i.e. the unit's `id` field, which for a drizzle migration is its bare filename. It MUST NOT be invented, guessed, or copied from this addendum: this addendum deliberately does NOT name it, because the migration ordinal is globally contested and naming it here would freeze an allocation this lane has no authority to make.
THE_ID.derived_position: It MUST be appended at the position DERIVED from the unit's position in BASELINE_UNITS, because all three lists are produced by filtering or iterating BASELINE_UNITS in order and therefore inherit that order. For a unit appended at the END of BASELINE_UNITS - the expected shape for a new highest-ordinal drizzle migration - the derived position is LAST. The implementing mission MUST derive this from the measured BASELINE_UNITS order and MUST NOT assume 'last' without measuring: BASELINE_UNITS interleaves policy units at ordinals 44-49, so filename order and manifest order are NOT the same relation.
THE_ID.closed_world_preserved: All three comparisons MUST remain exact ordered closed-world comparisons. Control C's guard `evidence.dmlUnits.length !== EXPECTED_DML_UNITS.length || evidence.dmlUnits.some((id, i) => id !== EXPECTED_DML_UNITS[i])` MUST retain BOTH conjuncts; dropping the length check alone would silently accept a longer list.
